transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time to discuss the eighth-grade civics oral-history project. Before we can move forward, I want to make sure we've thoroughly reviewed the draft plan through our standard approval process. I have some concerns I'd like us to work through together — particularly around student privacy, the use of personal phones for audio recording, publishing all recordings on the public school website, and retaining those files indefinitely. Let's start by hearing from each of you on what you see in this proposal.

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. Here's what my project roster review turned up. The draft plan calls for 20 student interviewers, but my review of the roster shows that exactly eight students have completed the district's media-ethics training: J1, J3, J6, J8, J11, J14, J17, and J20. Under our district's requirements, only those eight students may conduct recorded interviews. Additionally, the approval file must include a training-verification record for each of these students before interviews can begin. So the plan will need to be revised to reflect that only these eight trained students are eligible to serve as interviewers, and we'll need to include the training-verification documentation in the approval packet.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Ms. Patel. Now let me share my family-consent review findings. I reviewed the consent forms for all twenty proposed interviewees, and I found that five interviewees — I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 — have not granted permission for public web publication of their recordings. Their consent forms specify that their recordings may be used only in the school's internal archive, not on the public school website. The plan must be revised so that recordings for these five interviewees are excluded from public web publication and retained only in the internal archive. Additionally, the approval file must include a consent-exclusion record documenting that these five interviewees declined public web publication permission, so we have a clear audit trail of which recordings may and may not be posted publicly.

transcript.text: Thank you, Ms. Patel and Mr. Lewis. Now let me share my technology review findings. My review confirms that personal phones cannot be used for school recordings. The project must use district tablets instead. All audio files must be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive — not on personal devices or general school servers. Regarding retention, recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation — indefinite retention is not permitted. Finally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record documenting that the restricted drive is properly configured before interviews can begin. These requirements will need to be incorporated into the revised plan and the approval packet.
